claims.text: A page exists at /docs/support/provider-support-policy/ (the Provider support policy page linked from the support index).
Pulumi's provider support policy page describes how long Pulumi maintains each provider major version.
Some Pulumi providers get long-term security updates, and the provider support policy page identifies which ones.
Pulumi focuses on actively supporting the latest released major version of the providers it maintains.
For a set of widely used providers, Pulumi ships security updates for the previous major version for up to a year, or until the next major version is released, whichever comes first.
The page /docs/support/provider-support-policy/ exists and lists the covered providers and what a long-term support release contains.
Older major versions of Pulumi-maintained providers receive no patches at all.
The Pulumi Registry (/registry/) lists the current version for all providers maintained by Pulumi.
Pulumi does not automatically roll back changes during an update on error or failure; it completes pending in-progress operations, then exits and reports the error.
Pulumi does not query the cloud provider's live state before pulumi up or pulumi preview by default.
`pulumi up --refresh` refreshes and applies desired state in a single step.
Pulumi Cloud provides built-in drift detection for scheduled automated drift detection and remediation.
Pulumi auto-naming appends a random suffix to the logical name, and this lets Pulumi replace resources with less downtime by creating the replacement before deleting the old one.
Pulumi Cloud manages a unique encryption key per stack, so encrypting the same value in two stacks yields different encrypted strings.
Pulumi does not use the Terraform engine; some Pulumi providers use Terraform schemas, whereas Pulumi native providers map directly to cloud provider APIs and do not use Terraform schemas.
Experimental Pulumi features are always opt-in and can change or be removed at any time without a deprecation cycle; PULUMI_EXPERIMENTAL=true enables experimental functionality.
The tilde operator in npm (~1.2.3) allows patch updates on the current minor version.
Each major version of a Pulumi provider includes migration logic to smooth upgrade from the immediately previous major version, but these migrations do not always work across multiple major versions.
Pulumi actively maintains the latest released major version of every provider it publishes.
For a set of widely used providers, Pulumi ships security updates for the previous major version (N-1) for up to 12 months, or until the next major version is released, whichever comes first.
The providers receiving Pulumi long-term support updates are AWS, Azure Classic, Azure Native, Azure AD, Command, Docker Build, GCP, Kubernetes, TLS, and Vault.
Registry package pages exist at /registry/packages/ for aws, azure, azure-native, azuread, command, docker-build, gcp, kubernetes, tls, and vault.

The Pulumi provider LTS branch ships High/Critical CVE security patches, including fixes for CVEs affecting the provider's code or direct dependencies and fixes for broken internal infrastructure on the LTS branch needed to ship them.

A Pulumi provider LTS release does not contain new upstream API versions, new resources or properties, performance improvements, non-security bug fixes, or compatibility with newer language runtime versions.
LTS provider releases remain compatible with the Pulumi engine version they were frozen at, unless security fixes prompt otherwise.
Exactly one long-term support major version exists per covered provider at any time.
When major N+1 ships, N becomes the new current major, the old N becomes the new LTS major, and the previous LTS major reaches end of life the same day regardless of remaining 12-month window.
Within the LTS major, only the latest minor version receives patches; earlier minors are frozen.
LTS provider releases are available through the same standard package registries as current-major releases but are tagged differently.
Customers pinning to a specific major version (recommended) automatically receive patch releases as they ship.
Older majors than the LTS version receive no patches; if v3 is newest, v2 is N-1 and v1 and earlier are end of life.
The current major (N) receives new features, new resources, bug fixes, security patches, dependency upgrades, and new upstream API versions until N+1 ships.
End-of-life versions (N-2 and older) are not supported and receive no updates.
The Pulumi support FAQ at /docs/support/faq/infrastructure/ contains a section 'what-are-the-best-practices-for-maintaining-provider-versions'.
Pages exist at /registry/ and /docs/support/getting-support/.
